sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Live-cell staining of transfected HEK293 cells with an antibody against the extracellular epitope confirmed surface expression of full-length PLXDC2 (L2, L3). No functional assay result for the tagged construct is reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly states the epitope tag is placed after the secretion signal at the N-terminus of full-length PLXDC2, which by the authoritative landmarks corresponds to insert_after_residue=30 (last residue of the signal peptide, G) and residue_after=31 (K, first residue of the mature ectodomain). Python lookup confirmed aa(30)=G and aa(31)=K. The junction is 425 residues from the TM boundary (456), well clear of any steric constraint. L2 and L3 independently confirm the tag is surface-accessible by live-cell staining in the same system. Full-length, membrane-anchored PLXDC2 expressed in HEK293 cells with an epitope tag engineered immediately after the secretion signal (residues 1–30), placing it at the extracellular N-terminus of the mature protein. L2 and L3 (same paper) confirm the tag is accessible on the cell surface by live-cell staining.

sources.claim: All constructs have the epitope tag engineered after the secretion signal at the N-terminus.

literature_notes: All three ledger lines (L1, L2, L3) derive from the same paper (PMC4303762) and collectively describe a single site: an epitope tag placed immediately after the signal peptide cleavage site at the extracellular N-terminus of full-length, membrane-anchored PLXDC2. No internal loop insertions, C-terminal tags, or any other positions are mentioned in the ledger. The tag type is described only as 'epitope tag' in the available clips; the specific tag identity (e.g., FLAG, HA) is not resolvable from the ledger alone. L3 also notes that the same N-terminal tag strategy was applied to PLXDC2-dC (intracellular domain-deleted) and ECD-deleted constructs, but those truncations do not constitute additional surface-tag sites for full-length PLXDC2.
